rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->Nobody taught Wren the lay of the roads. It arrived: a month after a beggar went down the cistern stairs and did not come up, she opened her mouth in a common room and the crown verses came out of it. She sings the fifth with her eyes closed, cannot translate a line of it, and it stops in the same place every time.
A chorister held that verse in a cellar for eight centuries. A beggar carried it up a flooded stair and died on the way. Wren would like to know whether she is a bard with a good ear or the next person it picked up.
The brothers of the Silent Monastery took in the fourth rider at their gate and wrote down what he sang while he was dying, words and all. Find their songbook and read the staves.

node.label: The staves run out
node.text: The house songbook holds the lay of the five roads, set down from a dying rider at the gate. Four verses end. The fifth stops mid-phrase, with ruled staves left blank after it for an ending.\n\nWren should see this.

li.label: Not a curse. An unfinished song.
li.text: The rider refused to give the brothers the fifth verse's ending, on the grounds that it had not happened yet. When the fifth road ends, he said, whoever is standing there will know how it goes.\n\nWren has the copied pages in her lute case. She is waiting for the end of a road.

rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->Hew and Gille took Iron Brand arrows at the north ford, and Madoc closed his hand on a fire so that they would be warm. He has not opened it since. It has been burning over them ever since, small and steady, three weeks east of wherever the company happens to be.

It costs him almost nothing. Almost nothing, every minute, since the day he set it, and tonight the bill arrived: the best fire shaper any of them has met cannot keep an ordinary campfire flickering.

There is nothing on the other end of this and no bargain to close. There is a man who has to decide to open his hand, and who cannot decide it without saying out loud what he has been doing.

li.label: That is that
li.text:
Madoc said the whole of it out loud: the two men at the ford, and the fire he has held over them since. Then he opened his hand, and three weeks east, that flame went out.
He lays fires with a flint now, like anybody, and what he does with them he does exactly, first time.

li.label: Terrible hour for grammar
li.text:
Madoc chose to keep holding the fire at the ford.
Everything he does with a flame from here is done by a man doing something else at the same time. Most of it works. Some of it works far better than it should, and nobody can say in advance which.

rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->Raiders cut Bran off from the Wayfarer camp and he spent twelve days alone in a border ruin. On the fourth day something began hitting the cellar door from the inside, and it went on for the better part of two days, and he sat in the corner with his sword across his knees and did not open it.

It could have been raiders. They had run him into that ruin and they knew the ground. He has made that argument to himself about four hundred times and it is a good one.

It could also have been Hesk, the company's bowman, cut off in the same push. Serra thinks the pass took him. Bran has never said otherwise.

The ruin is three days back down the pass.

li.label: Six days
li.text:
The cellar door was under the ruin's collapsed north end. The party dug it clear and freed Hesk, alive after six days in the dark. The beam across the door could not have been moved from below.

Bran spent twelve days at that ruin and never checked the pile. He could not have known what was under it, which is not the same as not being able to find out.

The bowman goes home to Thornden, under his own name.

rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->One of Maewyn's ravens has come back thin, carrying a sprig of sagewort gone to seed. It flowers in spring; it should not have seed on it in any year she is there.

Both birds have been flying home every few weeks all this time to look at a house with nobody in it. Nobody has cut anything since she left. The hives will swarm and die without a hand on them, and nine kinds of physic that grow nowhere else in the valley are going under mint and weed.

She said the hills could hold it a while. A while has turned out to have a length.

Go back to the grove.

li.label: A list on the inside of a door
li.text: The grove goes to a girl from the valley farm who has been walking up the hill to watch the bees since she was nine.\n\nMaewyn spent two days on the handover: the swarming hive split, instructions scratched inside the door, and two years of teaching by raven promised. What survives is nine kinds of physic that would otherwise stop existing in this valley.

li.label: Gorse in four years
li.text: Maewyn closed the grove: opened the hives, took one small box from the black bed, and laid the door flat in the grass so nothing would have to break in. Gorse in four years, she says. Birch after that.\n\n"It was on loan and I have handed it back, and that is the correct end of the arrangement."
